prompt:
Create a fresh finished square fantasy RPG WORLD MAP of Vladimir's Elsewhere. Image 1 is ONLY the visual STYLE/QUALITY reference: match its richly colored hand-painted anime fantasy map finish, beautifully sculpted terrain, delicate readable little buildings, lush tree masses, brilliant blues and greens, warm light and fine illustrative detail. Do NOT copy Glowhaven's circular city, Evertree, academies, coastline or mountains. No old map layout is binding. Invent a delightful, surprising organic composition.
This is an eccentric immortal wizard's private pocket-world: a whole lush garden valley of living curiosities and impossible hobby pavilions, small compared with a country but broad enough for winding walks and discovery. High sweeping oblique aerial map view with the WHOLE private realm visible, terrain and roof forms readable; sparse or no horizon. Rich emerald groves, turquoise streams and pools, warm meadows, unusual luminous glass-root plants, sculptural rock shelves and small fantastical buildings. A continuous winding copper-lantern walk and covered arcades join all the places across gentle garden levels, stream bridges and stairs. Quiet natural spaces separate landmarks. Be CREATIVE with the landforms and the arrangement. Locations may be placed wherever composition and discovery work best. Avoid rigid rows, a dollhouse of rectangular rooms, a cutaway shopping arcade or a unified purple-roof palace. It should feel like an enchanting explorable landscape assembled around a very particular person's obsessions.
Include eight main places with STRONGLY DIFFERENT silhouettes, organically distributed:
- Shifting Gallery: a long cream arched gallery sweeping around one garden slope; brass rails let several arch segments slide sideways. At its welcoming entrance stands one large copper lantern beside a single private return doorway. It is the only gate out. No huge castle.
- Glassroot Gardens: an open grove of fantastical TRANSPARENT glasslike roots and lilac foliage arching around clear stillwater pools and clipped paths. Tiny floating manta-ray shapes and a few antlered hares may suggest peaceful magical ecology. A garden, not a giant greenhouse capsule.
- Inverted Court: an exposed gravity-defying stone court with a striking fountain flowing UP into an overhead circular basin, an ascending stair that curls up a wall, clear railings and normal safe approaches. Keep this local marvel isolated from the ordinary streams.
- Porcelain Workshops: a charming asymmetrical workshop cluster of cream ceramic walls, warm terracotta/copper roofs and broad open work bays; small brass machinery, repair benches and pale inert articulated frames visible at map scale. Its real craft function should read, not a throne room.
- The Little Kingdom: a whimsical open-sided timber games pavilion with an enormous clearly RAISED tabletop holding one tiny clockwork valley, painted toy villages, miniature bridges and little carriages. The miniature rests visibly on a table; it must not become a second full-size city. A kite hangs beside its balcony.
- Tilt Court: a playful open-air emerald-blue ringball playing platform in a modest architectural enclosure, at a jaunty safe tilt, with several brass hoops, padded margins and a small players' bench. Not an arena or tournament stadium.
- Rainward Orchard: a real flowering fruit orchard on gentle terraces with a small potting shed and sheltered bench; a narrow band of diagonal rain crosses one row while vertical rain falls beside it, sunlight touching dry paths. No enormous storm over the whole map.
- Cabinet of Evenings: an unusual tall narrow observation lodge with a curved viewing balcony and a fan of luminous glazed windows, displaying sunset amber, violet twilight, starry indigo and rainy teal skies simultaneously. These are window views rather than extra doorways or portals.
Give the garden paths a graceful irregular circuit with obvious junctions and usable bridges. Every landmark is reachable on foot back to the entry gallery. No isolated island rooms or lethal route gaps. Varied roofs and materials, indoor spaces suggested through generous openings where needed. Useful exquisite detail concentrated on the eight sites; quiet landscape between. Luminous magical atmosphere and wonder, no uniformly cold or purple grading. Coherent built foundations, individual walls and roofs, convincing streams and banks, continuous railings. Crisp purposeful drawn forms and selective architectural detail without grain, scratchy foliage, speckles, blurry pseudo-detail or excessive bloom. No named characters, no humanoid statues, no battles, no giant boss, no additional major sites. NO labels, names, lettering, numbers, title, compass, frame, legend, grid, pins, UI or watermark.
